newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rice prices seen steady on low exports.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rice prices seen steady on low exports.

text.p: Pakistani rice export prices are likely to remain steady in the next trading week beginning on Saturday on reduced demand from abroad, dealers said on Thursday.
"The prices remained steady in the week ended on Thursday as there are no major foreign buyers," an official at the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan said.

"The crop is good and it is not less than last year's," the official said. The 1996/97 (July-June) crop was estimated at 3.5 million tonnes, compared with 3.47 million in 1995/96 and 4.02 million in 1994/95.
The export prices of the superior Basmati variety and the IRRI-6 variety were unchanged at last week's $500 and $240 per tonne FOB respectively, the official said.
In the first quarter to September, Pakistan exported 244,757 tonnes of rice worth $81 million, compared to 207,791 tonnes worth $74 million in the year-ago period.
In September, rice exports fell to 74,748 tonnes worth $24 million, compared to 97,779 tonnes worth $31 million in August and 72,484 tonnes worth $27 million in September 1995.
